tone: warm, thankful, prayerful, confident in the gospel, and centered on God's saving action in His Son
target_reader: religion-naive adults and older adolescents near grade 6
translation_identity: firmly dynamic-equivalence, NLT-like in readability but independent
test_purpose: Fresh Engine 2.2 passage-sense-resolution drafting of Colossians 1:1-14

sealed_context.instruction: Translate from the Greek and the completed source-side passage-sense brief only. Do not reconstruct, imitate, or refer to previous FLT wording, previous candidates, comparison translations, or conversation drafts.

governing_rules: Passage-sense resolution precedes English composition. Follow the completed source-side brief and expose genuinely viable alternatives in the review apparatus.
All three candidates pursue the same constitutional goal; no provider receives a readability, fidelity, or blended specialty.
Write natural English that a religion-naive adult can follow on one hearing. The main assertion should arrive before the listener loses it.
Build English sentences and paragraphs rather than preserving Greek clause architecture. Split, combine, reorder, or unpack when comprehension benefits.
Actively avoid stacked clauses, overloaded breaths, preposition clusters, delayed subjects or main verbs, abstract-noun chains, embedded explanation, and translated-sounding prose.
Vary English transitions when needed for the ear, but preserve deliberate repetition, escalation, metaphor, emphasis, and connective logic.
Preserve every material proposition; cause, contrast, purpose, result, and sequence; meaningful ambiguity; agency, force, certainty, and key-term links.
The prose serves the reader; notes serve accountability. Do not leave the reading text opaque and expect a footnote to supply material meaning.
Keep candidate alternatives in the review apparatus, not in brackets in the reading text, unless the human editor later decides otherwise.
Propose notes for literal-source transparency, meaningful word-family links, metaphors hidden by dynamic rendering, and disputed constructions.
Footnotes disclose translation decisions and establish critical trust; they are not apologies for, or repairs to, an inadequate reading text.
No comparison translations, traditional benchmark wording, prior FLT wording, prior candidates, editor benchmark, conversation drafts, or sealed human wording may enter blind drafting.
Record oral-design moves and remaining oral risks; do not claim that a drafting worker has certified its own oral quality.
existing_decisions: Render theological vocabulary contextually in reader-facing English; do not preserve opaque church terms merely because they are traditional.
Use brothers and sisters when the context addresses the whole church and the Greek plural is inclusive.
Render saints contextually as God's holy people when it denotes the Christian community.
Render diakonos by its contextual function rather than automatically importing the opaque title minister or deacon.

Footnotes may disclose disputed constructions, traditional glosses, cultural force, literal wording, and source-language links, but may not compensate for material meaning missing from the reading text.
Preserve contextual links across accepted units without importing or reopening their accepted English wording during blind drafting.
The human editor alone selects, synthesizes, approves smoothing changes, and finalizes wording.

matrix_alerts.neutral_range: faith, trust, faithfulness; faithful or believing
matrix_alerts.instruction: Use natural reader-facing English while preserving the distinction between the Colossians' trust in Christ in verse 4 and the faithful or believing description in verse 2.

matrix_alerts.neutral_range: hope, confident expectation, or the future good expected
matrix_alerts.instruction: In verse 5 make clear that hope substantially denotes the future good kept for the believers and that it grounds their faith and love.
Prefer transparent reader-facing language and preserve the message's worldwide fruit-bearing and growth.

matrix_alerts.neutral_range: grace, generous favor, or undeserved kindness
matrix_alerts.instruction: Retain grace when the context and note apparatus can make its meaning clear; do not reduce it to generic kindness.

matrix_alerts.neutral_range: knowledge, full knowledge, recognition, or deep understanding
matrix_alerts.instruction: Preserve the movement from truly knowing God's grace in verse 6 to knowing His will in verse 9 and growing in knowing God in verse 10 without forcing identical English forms.
Render the metaphor dynamically as lived conduct unless a literal note materially helps transparency.

matrix_alerts.neutral_range: release, freedom, rescue by payment, or redemption
matrix_alerts.instruction: Let the following explanation, forgiveness of sins, control the reader-facing wording while exposing the traditional term or release sense in the apparatus.

units.title: Greeting, thanksgiving for the gospel's fruit, and prayer for a life that pleases the Lord
known_issues: Verses 1-2 form the greeting; verses 3-8 form the thanksgiving; verses 9-14 form the prayer and its saving climax.
Verse 2 addresses one mixed Christian community. Faithful and believing are both viable senses of pistos.
Verses 4-5 state that the Colossians' trust and love exist because of the hope kept for them; hope substantially denotes the awaited future good, not merely a hopeful attitude.
The good news bears fruit and grows in verse 6, and the same imagery returns in the believers' good works and knowledge of God in verse 10.
Verse 7 follows the SBLGNT reading hyper hemon: Epaphras serves Christ on our behalf. A reader note should disclose the variant your behalf.
Verse 8 can mean love produced by the Holy Spirit or spiritual love; the Holy Spirit reading is primary but the alternative remains viable.
Verses 9-10 connect knowing God's will to living in a way that honors and pleases the Lord; knowledge is not presented as an end in itself.
Verses 11-12 leave open whether with joy modifies endurance and patience or the following thanksgiving.
Verse 12 says the Father qualified you; verse 13 broadens to us. Preserve the shift without making qualification sound earned.
Verse 14 explains redemption or release as forgiveness of sins and does not contain through His blood in the SBLGNT reading.
Do not import accepted Philippians wording into blind drafting, even where themes or vocabulary overlap.

verses.greek: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς
τοῖς ἐν Κολοσσαῖς ἁγίοις καὶ πιστοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν
Εὐχαριστοῦμεν τῷ θεῷ πατρὶ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι
ἀκούσαντες τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ἣν ἔχετε εἰς πάντας τοὺς ἁγίους
διὰ τὴν ἐλπίδα τὴν ἀποκειμένην ὑμῖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἣν προηκούσατε ἐν τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας τοῦ εὐαγγελίου
τοῦ παρόντος εἰς ὑμᾶς καθὼς καὶ ἐν παντὶ τῷ κόσμῳ ἐστὶν καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον καθὼς καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν ἀφ’ ἧς ἡμέρας ἠκούσατε καὶ ἐπέγνωτε τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ
καθὼς ἐμάθετε ἀπὸ Ἐπαφρᾶ τοῦ ἀγαπητοῦ συνδούλου ἡμῶν ὅς ἐστιν πιστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν διάκονος τοῦ Χριστοῦ
ὁ καὶ δηλώσας ἡμῖν τὴν ὑμῶν ἀγάπην ἐν πνεύματι
Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφ’ ἧς ἡμέρας ἠκούσαμεν οὐ παυόμεθα ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν προσευχόμενοι καὶ αἰτούμενοι ἵνα πληρωθῆτε τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ καὶ συνέσει πνευματικῇ
περιπατῆσαι ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου εἰς πᾶσαν ἀρεσκείαν ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ ἀγαθῷ καρποφοροῦντες καὶ αὐξανόμενοι τῇ ἐπιγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ
ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει δυναμούμενοι κατὰ τὸ κράτος τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ εἰς πᾶσαν ὑπομονὴν καὶ μακροθυμίαν μετὰ χαρᾶς
εὐχαριστοῦντες τῷ πατρὶ τῷ ἱκανώσαντι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν μερίδα τοῦ κλήρου τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ φωτί
ὃς ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ σκότους καὶ μετέστησεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ
ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν

passage_sense_resolution.prepared_from: SBLGNT text, parsed morphology, local discourse, source-language analysis, and governing FLT rules; no comparison translation or prior FLT English
passage_argument: Paul and Timothy greet the Colossian believers with grace and peace from God their Father.
They thank God because the Colossians trust Christ and love God's people, a response grounded in the future good kept for them and announced in the true good news.
That message is present among them and throughout the world, bearing fruit and growing from the day they truly understood God's grace through Epaphras.
Epaphras's report leads Paul and Timothy to pray that the believers will fully know God's will and therefore live in a way that honors and pleases the Lord.
Such a life bears fruit, grows in knowing God, receives divine strength for endurance, and joyfully gives thanks for the Father's rescue and the forgiveness found in His Son.

proposition_map.statement: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and Timothy address the holy and faithful or believing family in Colossae and bless them with grace and peace from God their Father.

Paul and Timothy thank God when praying for the Colossians because their trust in Christ and love for God's people arise from the future hope announced by the true good news, which bears fruit and grows worldwide and which they learned through Epaphras, who reported their Spirit-produced love.

They continually ask God to fill the believers with knowledge of His will so they will live to please the Lord, bear fruit, know God more deeply, receive strength for joyful endurance, thank the Father for their inheritance, and recognize His rescue into the Son's kingdom where they have forgiveness.

expressions.source_expression: τοῖς ... ἁγίοις καὶ πιστοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἐν Χριστῷ
expressions.contextual_function: One coordinated description of the mixed Christian community in Colossae as holy and pistos brothers and sisters in Christ.
expressions.primary_sense: God's holy and faithful brothers and sisters who belong to Christ.
viable_alternatives: God's holy and believing brothers and sisters in Christ.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The single article governs the coordinated description, and the plural family term includes the whole church.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Use God's holy people or similarly clear community language and make the inclusive family address audible without suggesting two groups.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Disclose that faithful can also mean believing here and that the plural family address includes both men and women.
expressions.choice_risks: Faithful can imply proven reliability; believing foregrounds response to the gospel but may weaken the ethical overtone.

expressions.contextual_function: The adverb can attach most naturally to the thanksgiving or to the praying expression.
expressions.primary_sense: We always thank God when we pray for you.
viable_alternatives: We thank God whenever we pray for you.
expressions.discourse_evidence: Word order permits either scope, while the thanksgiving formula and natural discourse favor habitual thanks during prayer.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Choose one unambiguous natural English scope without turning the sentence into a claim of uninterrupted prayer.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: A note is optional because both readings express habitual prayerful thanksgiving.
expressions.choice_risks: Always can sound continuous in English; whenever can shift emphasis from constancy to occasion.

expressions.source_expression: τὴν πίστιν ... καὶ τὴν ἀγάπην ... διὰ τὴν ἐλπίδα τὴν ἀποκειμένην ὑμῖν ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς
expressions.contextual_function: The because phrase grounds both the Colossians' trust in Christ and their love for God's people in the hope securely stored for them.
expressions.primary_sense: You trust Christ and love all God's people because of the future good God has safely kept for you in heaven.
viable_alternatives: Your faith and love spring from the confident hope waiting for you in heaven.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The causal phrase follows both coordinated objects and hope is described as laid away for them, making the expected good prominent.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Make the causal link easy to hear and render hope concretely enough that a religion-naive reader does not hear mere optimism.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Explain that hope here includes the future good believers confidently expect because God keeps it for them.
expressions.choice_risks: Future good clarifies the object but partially unpacks the noun; confident hope preserves the term but may still sound subjective.

expressions.source_expression: τῷ λόγῳ τῆς ἀληθείας τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ... καρποφορούμενον καὶ αὐξανόμενον
expressions.contextual_function: The true good-news message has arrived among the Colossians and is bearing fruit and growing worldwide; the imagery returns in their conduct in verse 10.
expressions.primary_sense: The true good news is spreading, bearing fruit, and growing in the world and among the Colossians.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The message is the grammatical subject of the participles, and the paired imagery recurs when Paul describes believers' good works and knowledge of God.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Keep both fruit and growth visible and make clear that the message's effects, not a physical object, are spreading.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: A note is optional; preserve the verse 6 and verse 10 literary link in wording or apparatus.
expressions.choice_risks: Spreading is an explanatory addition; omitting it can make the worldwide statement awkward to hear.

expressions.source_expression: ἐπέγνωτε τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ
expressions.contextual_function: The phrase can describe genuinely understanding God's grace or understanding the truth about God's grace.
viable_alternatives: You understood the truth about God's grace.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The adverbial phrase can qualify the manner of knowing or characterize the grace-message as truth.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Choose a natural English construction that keeps both real understanding and the truth of the message in view as far as possible.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Disclose the viable truth-about-God's-grace reading if the reading text selects genuinely understood.
expressions.choice_risks: Truly can sound like an assessment of sincerity; truth about can make grace sound merely informational.

expressions.source_expression: ὅς ἐστιν πιστὸς ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν διάκονος τοῦ Χριστοῦ
expressions.contextual_function: Epaphras faithfully serves Christ on Paul and Timothy's behalf; diakonos identifies his service function.
expressions.primary_sense: He faithfully serves Christ on our behalf.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The SBLGNT reads hemon, our, while a significant variant reads hymon, your; the immediate speakers are Paul and Timothy.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Follow our behalf and use transparent service language rather than an unexplained church title.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: State that some manuscripts read on your behalf instead of on our behalf.
expressions.choice_risks: Representative can overdefine his role; servant can obscure that he carries out ministry on behalf of others.

expressions.contextual_function: The prepositional phrase most likely identifies the Holy Spirit as the sphere or source of their love, though spiritual love is possible.
expressions.primary_sense: the love the Holy Spirit has produced in you
expressions.discourse_evidence: Paul commonly uses Spirit language for divine agency, while the anarthrous noun and compact phrase leave a qualitative reading grammatically possible.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Make the Holy Spirit's role clear if selecting the primary sense, without implying coercion or erasing the Colossians' active love.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Disclose that the phrase can also mean your spiritual love.
expressions.choice_risks: Produced can sound mechanistic; spiritual love is concise but vague and can hide divine agency.

expressions.source_expression: ἵνα πληρωθῆτε τὴν ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ ... περιπατῆσαι ἀξίως τοῦ κυρίου
expressions.contextual_function: Full knowledge of God's will has the intended result of conduct that honors the Lord and pleases Him in every way.
expressions.primary_sense: We ask God to help you fully know His will so that you will live in a way that honors and pleases the Lord.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The infinitive of conduct depends on the prayer request and introduces the practical purpose or result developed in the following participles.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Bring the purpose connection forward in natural English and render walk as life or conduct for first-hearing clarity.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: A note is optional unless the reading text substantially expands spiritual wisdom and understanding.
expressions.choice_risks: Worthy can sound merit-based or obscure; honors preserves relational fitness but is an interpretive unpacking.

expressions.contextual_function: The dative can identify the sphere of growth in knowing God or the means by which believers grow.
expressions.primary_sense: growing as you know God better
viable_alternatives: growing through your knowledge of God
expressions.discourse_evidence: The dative permits both sphere and means, and the nearby fruit-and-growth imagery connects knowledge with lived transformation.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Use personal language about knowing God rather than an abstract noun chain, while retaining the growth link to verse 6.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Disclose the through knowing God alternative if it would materially affect interpretation.
expressions.choice_risks: Know God better is relationally clear but can sound merely cognitive; through knowledge may make knowledge mechanically causal.

expressions.source_expression: εἰς πᾶσαν ὑπομονὴν καὶ μακροθυμίαν μετὰ χαρᾶς εὐχαριστοῦντες
expressions.contextual_function: With joy can modify endurance and patience or introduce the following act of thanksgiving.
expressions.primary_sense: strength for joyful endurance and patience, while giving thanks to the Father
viable_alternatives: strength for endurance and patience, and joyfully giving thanks to the Father
expressions.discourse_evidence: SBLGNT punctuation attaches the phrase to endurance, but punctuation is editorial and the participial sequence allows attachment to thanksgiving.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Choose a phrasing whose attachment is clear to the ear and that does not imply forced cheerfulness during suffering.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Explain the alternate attachment because it changes whether joy characterizes endurance or thanksgiving.
expressions.choice_risks: Joyful endurance may sound emotionally prescriptive; joyfully thanking may weaken the tone of empowered perseverance.

expressions.source_expression: τῷ ἱκανώσαντι ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν μερίδα τοῦ κλήρου τῶν ἁγίων ἐν τῷ φωτί
expressions.contextual_function: The Father made the believers fit to share in the allotted inheritance belonging to God's holy people in the realm of light.
expressions.primary_sense: The Father made you fit to share the inheritance He gives His people who live in the light.
viable_alternatives: The Father qualified you to receive your share of His holy people's inheritance in the light.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The Father is the agent of hikanos, and the overlapping share, lot, and inheritance terms evoke a divinely assigned portion rather than earned eligibility.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Keep the Father's action primary, avoid bureaucratic qualified language if possible, and preserve the shared inheritance and light imagery.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Explain that the Greek combines the ideas of receiving a share and an allotted inheritance, with light contrasting the darkness of verse 13.
expressions.choice_risks: Made fit can sound moralistic; qualified can sound administrative; live in the light may over-specify the compact phrase.

expressions.source_expression: ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς ἐκ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ σκότους καὶ μετέστησεν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἀγάπης αὐτοῦ
expressions.contextual_function: The Father decisively rescued us from darkness's ruling authority and transferred us into the kingdom ruled by His beloved Son.
expressions.primary_sense: He rescued us from the rule of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The coordinated aorist verbs preserve two movements, out of one dominion and into another, with the Father as agent.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Preserve rescue, change of rule, and the Son's kingdom without turning the images into a detailed political or geographic scene.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: A note is optional; if beloved Son is expanded, disclose that the Greek says the Son of His love.
expressions.choice_risks: Power can sound merely supernatural rather than ruling authority; domain is precise but too formal for the target reader.

expressions.source_expression: ἐν ᾧ ἔχομεν τὴν ἀπολύτρωσιν τὴν ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν
expressions.contextual_function: In the Son believers possess apolytrosis, immediately explained appositionally as the forgiveness of sins.
expressions.primary_sense: In Him we have been set free: our sins are forgiven.
viable_alternatives: In Him we have redemption, the forgiveness of our sins.
expressions.discourse_evidence: The second noun phrase explains the first; the SBLGNT verse does not include the later expansion through His blood.
expressions.reading_text_guidance: Use clear release or freedom language or retain redemption only if the sentence itself or note makes the explanation accessible; do not add through His blood to the reading text.
expressions.literal_note_guidance: Explain that redemption means release or freedom here and that some later manuscripts add through His blood, words absent from the SBLGNT reading.
expressions.choice_risks: Set free may sound as though forgiveness exhausts every aspect of redemption; redemption is traditional but opaque to the target reader.
